title: Tier Lift: campaign template + technical conditions
content:
Purpose: a compact, actionable QBR + renewal/expansion campaign template oriented specifically at customers who are good candidates to move from hosted usage to Dedicated or Private (or add a premium SLA). This doc is intentionally lightweight so CSMs can copy, adapt, and run fast.

High-level hypothesis: customers crossing predictable usage/latency/cost thresholds will choose Dedicated or Private when we present: (a) measurable TCO improvement, (b) a straight migration path with minimal engineering lift, (c) a clear SLA uplift and compliance story. The campaign focuses on aligning technical owners + commercial decision-makers.

1) Pre-QBR data prep (owner: CSM, due -2 weeks)
- Pull usage and cost trends (last 60/90/180 days): tokens/day, peak TPS, average latency, error rate, monthly invoice delta.
- Identify 3 economists / technical ratios: cost per 1M tokens (current hosted), estimated cost per 1M tokens on Dedicated (baseline), projected ROI window (months to payback).
- Flags: security/compliance requirements (audit logs, KMS), data residency constraints, legal/regulatory blockers.
- Internal readouts: which internal teams need to be looped (solutions-eng, infra, legal) and rough ETA for technical validation calls.
- Suggested subject line for invite: "QBR: product performance + options to reduce inference unit costs"

2) QBR slide skeleton (CSM/AE editable)
- Slide 1: TL;DR (current ARR contribution, 90-day trend, ask: evaluate Dedicated/Private + premium SLA)
- Slide 2: Health signals at a glance (usage, latency P90, error %, active routes)
- Slide 3: Why now? (thresholds reached, upcoming product initiatives driving traffic, compliance trigger)
- Slide 4: Economics comparison (hosted vs Dedicated vs Private; three scenarios: conservative/likely/aggressive) — include assumptions clearly.
- Slide 5: Technical lift & migration plan (milestones: infra review, pilot cluster, smoke tests, rollout, rollback plan)
- Slide 6: SLA and operational differences (support tiers, on-call escalation, observability retention, SLOs)
- Slide 7: Success metrics & acceptance criteria (throughput, latency SLOs, cost delta, time to failover)
- Slide 8: Next steps + decision timeline (proposal deadline, procurement, kickoff)

3) Typical technical checklist to validate during discovery call (owner: solutions engineer)
- Current model variants in use (sizes, parameter counts, custom finetunes)
- Average and peak sequence lengths per route
- KV cache usage patterns (are we prefix-heavy?)
- Latency sensitivity per route (P50/P90/P99 targets)
- Batchability: are payloads amenable to batching? (yes/no + estimated batching factor)
- Data ingress/egress constraints (VPC peering, NAT, allowed IP ranges)
- Compliance needs: HIPAA, SOC2 type II, FedRAMP notes if raised
- Logging and telemetry retention needs (30/90/365 days)

4) A quick risk map (to include in QBR)
- Risk: Unexpected cost overrun -> Mitigation: proposed dedicated sizing + guardrail budget, autoscale rules, trial credits for first 30-60 days.
- Risk: Migration causes a transient regression in latency -> Mitigation: canary rollout + fallbacks to hosted model during pilot.
- Risk: Procurement delay -> Mitigation: interim bridge policy (burst reserved capacity) and SOW template.

5) Commercial constructs & sample offers (PMM/RevOps consult before finalize)
- Baseline reserved commit (6/12/24 months) with volume tiers, include a short break clause for first 60 days of pilot.
- Premium SLA add-on: response time guarantee + higher observability retention + 1:8 on-call ratio.
- Pilot package: 2-week pilot on a 0.5x dedicated slice with free migration support (solutions-eng hours included).

6) Outreach cadence (CSM + AE)
- Week 0: Data-backed QBR where we introduce economics and migration playbook. Ask for technical discovery.
- Week 1: Technical discovery w/ solutions eng (30–60 min). Deliver preliminary sizing.
- Week 2: Deep-dive + pilot scoping, agree acceptance criteria.
- Week 3–4: Pilot begins (2–4 week window) + weekly standing sync.
- Decision checkpoint at pilot end (present results vs acceptance criteria).

7) Communication snippets (email / Slack)
- Initial QBR invite (short): "Hi <Name>, quick QBR to review how your inference costs and latency have trended and explore options to lower unit cost while improving SLOs. 30 min?"
- Technical discovery ask: "Can you share the top 2 routes by token volume and the P90 latency targets for each? Solutions eng will use this to size a pilot."
- Pilot kickoff message: "Starting pilot tomorrow on dedicated slice. Expected cutover time window: <X>. We'll monitor P99s closely and have rollback plan."

8) Renewal & expansion tracker (copy into your tracker sheet)
- Customer: , ARR: , Renewal date: , Current monthly tokens: , Proposed commitment: , Pilot start: , Pilot end: , Decision date: , Stakeholders: (BUSINESS / TECH / LEGAL), Primary risks:, Status: (scoping / pilot / proposal / negotiation / closed-won / closed-lost)
- Notes on negotiation levers: contract term, on-boarding hours, credit for migration, SLA pricing, observability retention.

9) Acceptance criteria examples (pick 3–4 measurable outcomes)
- Cost: dedicated unit cost <= hosted baseline * 0.75 within 30 days post-migration.
- Latency: P99 stays within +/- 10% of pre-migration P99 for critical routes.
- Throughput: sustained target TPS achieved within one week of pilot start.
- Reliability: production error rate drops or remains flat.

10) Post-decision operational checklist (owner: SRE/Solutions)
- Provision dedicated cluster, validate network connectivity.
- Run synthetic load for 2x expected traffic for 30 minutes.
- Validate observability dashboards and alerting.
- Run a data residency and KMS key rotation test (if applicable).
- Hand-off doc to customer ops + internal runbook links.

Open questions / To refine
- How aggressive should pricing discounts be relative to committed volume vs expected uplift? (Finance input needed)
- Do we want a formal SLA template for mid-market customers or reserve full SLAs for enterprise only?
- Pilot sizing defaults (we currently use 0.5–1.0x of measured peak; confirm with serving runtime team).

Quick how-to: runbook copy/paste for CSMs
- Step 0: run data pull and fill renewal tracker row.
- Step 1: schedule QBR and attach slide skeleton.
- Step 2: book solutions-eng for discovery and share checklist.
- Step 3: after discovery, propose pilot & provide SOW + estimated timeline.
- Step 4: run pilot, document outcomes, schedule decision review.

Appendix: sample Slack threads & links (paste into QBR)
- Link to billing breakdown (internal report id): billing/2025/customer-<id>
- Confluence: migration-runbook-dedicated (internal)
- Jira epic: JIRA-CS-987 (migration epic)

Notes to self: keep the content modular. CSMs should be able to copy this doc as a single file into a customer QBR folder and then swap the numbers + linked artifacts. This is intentionally more tactical than canonical playbooks elsewhere — fast to reproduce in-week.
